articles.title: Comparative outcomes of Bernese periacetabular osteotomy in adolescents, young adults, and middle-aged adults : a minimum two-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Chen YH, Lee CC, Wu KW, Chen YH, Yao SH, Lee TL, et al.
articles.population: Patients with symptomatic hip dysplasia undergoing Bernese periacetabular osteotomy, stratified by age: adolescents (11-19 years), young adults (20-39 years), and middle-aged adults (40-57 years)
articles.sample_size: 68 patients (58 hips): 16 adolescents, 18 young adults, 14 middle-aged adults
articles.outcomes: Radiological parameters, complications, pain scores (VAS), and modified Harris Hip Score at minimum two years follow-up
articles.take_home: All age groups showed significant improvements in pain and hip function after surgery, with no major differences in outcomes between teenagers, young adults, and middle-aged patients. Middle-aged patients took longer for their bone to heal (13 months versus 6 months in younger groups), but this did not affect their final results.

articles.title: After-Hours Surgery Is Associated With Adverse Perioperative Outcomes Following Hemiarthroplasty for Femoral Neck Fracture.
articles.authors: Beckers G, Deuschle J, Bocker W, Holzapfel BM, Simon D, Lerchenberger M
articles.population: Patients undergoing cemented hemiarthroplasty for displaced femoral neck fracture
articles.outcomes: Operative time, intra-operative complications, blood loss, transfusion requirements, periprosthetic joint infection, delirium, revision surgery, and 30-day mortality
articles.take_home: Surgery performed after hours was linked to longer operating times, greater blood loss, higher transfusion needs, and increased risk of joint infection compared to daytime surgery. However, the delay from hospital admission to surgery and the type of surgeon training were not independently associated with worse outcomes or death.

articles.title: Outcomes after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with versus without lateral extra-articular tenodesis: A propensity-matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Rteil A, Jason K, Amirouche F
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with or without lateral extra-articular tenodesis
articles.outcomes: Early complications at 3-6 months (arthrofibrosis procedures, wound complications, opioid use, readmissions), subsequent meniscal surgery and ACL reconstruction at 1-2 years, knee osteoarthritis at 5 years
articles.take_home: Adding lateral extra-articular tenodesis to ACL reconstruction surgery was associated with more early complications including swelling procedures and wound problems, and higher rates of meniscal surgery and osteoarthritis up to 5 years after surgery, but did not reduce the need for repeat ACL surgery in the primary analysis. This suggests careful patient selection is needed when considering this additional procedure.

articles.title: Functional alignment robotic-assisted TKA improves clinical outcomes compared with conventional mechanical alignment TKA: A single-surgeon randomised controlled non-inferiority trial with 2-year follow-up.
articles.authors: Coenen R, Peeters A, Bollars P, Nathwani D, Albelooshi A, Ettinger MT, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Knee Society Score subdomains, Oxford Knee Score, Forgotten Joint Score, pain, quality of life, activity levels, and satisfaction at 2 years
articles.take_home: Robotic-assisted functional alignment knee replacement produced modestly better patient-reported outcomes than conventional mechanical alignment at 2 years, including better function, satisfaction, pain relief and quality of life scores. The improvements were small but statistically significant.

articles.title: Specific functional knee phenotypes are associated with increased osteoarthritis progression: A >/=10-year longitudinal study.
articles.authors: Song SJ, Lee HB, Park CH
articles.population: Patients with healthy knees or early osteoarthritis at baseline
articles.sample_size: 388 patients (764 knees at baseline; 511 knees analysed across 15 functional knee phenotype groups)
articles.outcomes: Osteoarthritis progression over minimum 10 years, defined as increase in Kellgren-Lawrence grade
articles.take_home: Certain combinations of knee bone alignment patterns significantly increase the risk of osteoarthritis getting worse over 10 years or more. The study found three specific alignment patterns had progression rates between 75% and 89%, compared with 52% in knees with neutral alignment.

articles.title: The role of generalised joint Laxity in anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Za P, Papalia GF, Caria C, Minelli M, Basciani S, Vasta S
articles.population: Patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction, with and without generalised joint laxity
articles.sample_size: 3905 patients across 13 studies (55% male, 45% female, mean age 27.5 years)
articles.outcomes: Graft failure rate, knee laxity tests (Lachman and pivot shift), International Knee Documentation Committee score, and Lysholm Knee Score
articles.take_home: People with generalised joint laxity who have ACL surgery have more residual knee laxity and slightly lower knee scores after surgery than those without laxity, but graft failure rates were similar between the groups. It remains unclear whether the extra laxity actually matters for how well patients do in practice.

articles.title: Postoperative outcomes after total knee arthroplasty in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients receiving semaglutide versus tirzepatide: a propensity score-matched national research network analysis.
articles.authors: Wu KA, Choudhury A, Wu JA, Shenoy DA, Song J, Mai E, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national research network database with propensity score matching
articles.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty who were taking either semaglutide or tirzepatide
articles.outcomes: Medical complications at 90 days, surgical complications at 180 days, individual complications including infection, blood clots, heart attack and stroke, emergency department visits and readmissions at 90 and 180 days, and revision surgery rates
articles.take_home: In diabetic patients having knee replacement surgery, those taking semaglutide and those taking tirzepatide had similar rates of complications and hospital visits in the six months after surgery. Both medications appear safe to continue around the time of knee replacement.

articles.title: Comparative quality, accuracy, and readability of large language model responses to patient questions about robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kolac UC, Sili MV, Karademir OM, Ayik G, Akkaya M, Cakmak G
articles.study_type: Comparative evaluation of artificial intelligence systems
articles.population: Not applicable - study evaluated large language model outputs rather than human participants
articles.outcomes: Information quality, clinical accuracy, understandability and readability of responses from four large language models (ChatGPT-o3, ChatGPT-5.2, Gemini 3 and DeepSeek) about robotic-assisted knee replacement surgery
articles.take_home: All four AI systems provided clinically accurate information about robotic-assisted knee replacement, but they varied in how well they explained information and in readability. These AI tools should be used alongside other patient information sources rather than relied upon alone.

articles.title: Preoperative GLP-1 receptor agonist use and outcomes after total hip arthroplasty: a matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Diab AR, Chang THW, Diab O, Kheir MM
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: 90-day medical complications including deep vein thrombosis and hospital readmission; mechanical complications and revision surgery at 1, 2, and 5 years
articles.take_home: Patients taking GLP-1 receptor agonist medicines before hip replacement had fewer blood clots and unplanned hospital readmissions in the first 90 days after surgery, with no increase in other complications or revision surgery rates up to 5 years. Further research is needed to understand why these medicines may reduce blood clots after surgery.

articles.title: Simultaneous versus staged-bilateral THA using a piriformis-preserving minimally-invasive posterolateral approach.
articles.authors: Martinez Lotti A, Barbaglia V, Buljubasich M, Albani Forneris AF, Slullitel PAI, Buttaro MA
articles.population: Patients undergoing bilateral total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Re-admissions, adverse events, total length of stay, complications
articles.take_home: Having both hip replacements in one operation is as safe as having them in two separate operations, but means you spend 2 days less in hospital overall. The risk of complications and needing to come back to hospital is similar either way.

articles.title: The Effect of Posterior Tibial Slope Change on Functional Outcomes After Posterior-Stabilized Total Knee Arthroplasty: An Analysis of 370 Patients Who Had A Minimum 4-Year Follow-Up.
articles.authors: Altun O, Ergisi Y, Ozdemir E, Ozihtiyar AA, Altintas M, Dasar U
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary cemented posterior-stabilized total knee replacement with minimum 4-year follow-up
articles.outcomes: Pain (Visual Analog Scale), function (Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index, Knee Society Score, Oxford Knee Score, Forgotten Joint Score-12), knee range of motion
articles.take_home: Small changes in the angle of the shin bone (posterior tibial slope) after knee replacement surgery do not meaningfully affect pain relief or how well patients function. How well patients do after surgery depends mainly on how well they were functioning before the operation.

articles.title: Intraoperative Assessment of Component Loosening in Hip Arthroplasty: An International Delphi Consensus.
articles.authors: Hopman AGM, Blankevoort L, Amanatullah DF, Lustig S, Schafroth MU, Kievit AJ
articles.population: Orthopaedic surgeons experienced in revision hip arthroplasty from 32 countries
articles.sample_size: 125 surgeons approached; 43 completed Round 1; 37 completed all three rounds
articles.outcomes: Agreement on standardised intraoperative methods for assessing component loosening in hip arthroplasty; consensus reached on 15 of 48 statements
articles.take_home: Experts agreed that visible movement of the hip component when the leg is moved in different directions is the key sign of a loose hip replacement during surgery. The study provides the first standardised framework for surgeons to assess loosening during revision operations.

articles.title: Proximal Femoral Replacement Outcomes for Oncologic Versus Non-Oncologic Indications: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Kurapatti M, Shah A, Tao B, Henriquez A, Parsons K, Wu K, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing proximal femoral replacement for oncologic or non-oncologic indications
articles.sample_size: 2,804 cases from 42 studies (2,081 oncologic and 723 non-oncologic)
articles.outcomes: Overall complication rate, dislocation, infection, aseptic loosening, periprosthetic fracture, revision rate, amputation rate, implant survivorship, patient survival
articles.take_home: Proximal femoral replacement has similar overall complication rates regardless of whether it is used for cancer or non-cancer reasons, but patients treated for non-cancer conditions need revision surgery more often, whilst those treated for cancer have higher death rates. Implant survival was 91% at one year, 89% at five years, and 77% at ten years.

articles.title: Intramedullary nailing compared with primary total hip arthroplasty for pertrochanteric fractures in autonomous elderly patients : a prospective randomized study.
articles.authors: Piercecchi A, Bordet A, Labattut L, Maczynski A, Baulot E, Martz P
articles.population: Autonomous elderly patients aged 70 years and older with pertrochanteric hip fractures
articles.sample_size: 69 patients (35 intramedullary nailing, 34 total hip arthroplasty)
articles.outcomes: Harris Hip Score at six months (primary outcome), functional recovery, pain, complications, and survival at up to 4.1 years median follow-up
articles.take_home: Both intramedullary nailing and total hip arthroplasty produced similar functional outcomes and survival rates in elderly patients with pertrochanteric fractures. Total hip arthroplasty took longer to perform but offered no clinically meaningful benefit to justify its routine use in this group.

articles.title: Association of preoperative flexion contracture and limited knee flexion with short-term patient-reported outcomes after medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kinoshita T, Bunyoz KI, Mortensen KRL, Jensen CB, Nielsen CS, Gromov K, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing mobile-bearing medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty for anteromedial osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Oxford Knee Score and Forgotten Joint Score-12 at 3, 12, and 24 months postoperatively
articles.take_home: Patients with mild stiffness before surgery (slight bend or reduced bending) recovered slightly more slowly in the first year, but by 2 years after surgery all patients achieved similar improvements in their knee function and symptoms regardless of how stiff their knee was beforehand.

articles.title: Implant migration and clinical outcomes with cemented vs cementless Motec cups in total trapeziometacarpal arthroplasty: a 10-year prospective RSA cohort study of 69 patients.
articles.authors: Rautio E, Stilling M, Hansen TB, Thillemann JK
articles.study_type: Prospective comparative cohort study with radiostereometric analysis
articles.population: Patients undergoing total trapeziometacarpal arthroplasty with Motec cups
articles.sample_size: 69 patients (22 cementless cups, 47 cemented cups); 13 with cup measurements at 10 years
articles.outcomes: Cup migration (radiostereometric analysis), revision rate, pain, grip strength, Disabilities of the Arm Shoulder and Hand score, patient satisfaction
articles.take_home: Both cemented and cementless Motec cups showed similar amounts of migration over 10 years, but cups that were later revised moved more than those that stayed in place. Patients whose implants were not revised reported good satisfaction and improvement in pain and function.

articles.title: Effect of exercise on bone health in middle aged and older adults: hierarchical network meta-analysis of randomised trials.
articles.authors: Lu C, Li L, Zhang L, Gao Q, Meng J, Xue Y, et al.
articles.study_type: Hierarchical Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
articles.population: Middle aged (40-60 years) and older adults (>60 years)
articles.sample_size: 124 trials with 18,429 participants (fracture analysis: 26 trials with 11,132 participants)
articles.outcomes: Changes in bone mineral density at lumbar spine, femoral neck, and total hip; fracture incidence
articles.take_home: Brisk walking or jogging and combined aerobic-resistance exercises probably help maintain bone density in middle aged and older adults. Doing around 2-3 hours of brisk walking or jogging per week may achieve meaningful bone health benefits, with some evidence that mixed aerobic and mind-body exercise might also reduce fracture risk.

articles.title: Age-Adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index Outperforms Other Comorbidity Measures in Predicting 90-Day Readmissions After Simultaneous Bilateral Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Tsai SW, Chang CY, Hung YT, Lee KH, Lin YK, Chen CF, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing simultaneous bilateral total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: 90-day readmissions (medical, surgical, infection-related), 1-year reoperations, and prolonged length of stay (8 days or more)
articles.take_home: The age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index was better at predicting which patients would need hospital readmission within 90 days after having both knees replaced at the same time compared to three other commonly used risk assessment tools. This index may help doctors identify high-risk patients before surgery.

articles.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Assessment of Muscle Damage After Postero-lateral Versus Supercapsular Percutaneously-Assisted Total Hip Approaches: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Gan F, Zhang Q, Luo H, Li L, Zheng F, Lin X, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary unilateral total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Quadratus femoris muscle fatty infiltration, atrophy and tendon integrity of periacetabular muscles, operative time, blood loss, incision size, pain (VAS), hip function (Harris Hip Score), and dislocations at 12 months
articles.take_home: The supercapsular minimally invasive approach better preserved the quadratus femoris muscle with less fatty infiltration and damage compared to the standard postero-lateral approach. Both approaches produced similar clinical outcomes at 12 months, although the minimally invasive approach had better early results but took longer and caused slightly more bleeding.

articles.title: Reducing the Surveillance Burden in Metal-on-Metal Hip Arthroplasties: A Risk-Adapted Three-Tier Model Based on a Large Patient Cohort.
articles.authors: Selim A, Saeed A, George A, Clarke M, Bonde S, Naseem S, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort analysis with risk prediction model development
articles.population: Patients with metal-on-metal hip resurfacings and large-head metal-on-metal total hip arthroplasties
articles.outcomes: Abnormal MRI findings or need for hip revision surgery
articles.take_home: A three-tier risk-adapted follow-up system can safely reduce unnecessary clinic visits and scans for metal-on-metal hip patients compared to current UK guidelines, whilst still identifying those at higher risk of problems. Low-risk patients may not need follow-up after 10 years unless they develop symptoms.

articles.title: Variation in the Use of Cemented Versus Uncemented Hemiarthroplasty and Total Hip Arthroplasty for Treatment of Femoral Neck Fractures in the United States.
articles.authors: Anderson PA, Greenwald A, Riley C, Kates SL, Jimenez E, Pezold R, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years and older with femoral neck fractures treated with hemiarthroplasty or total hip arthroplasty in the United States
articles.sample_size: 81,610 cases (66,328 hemiarthroplasties and 15,282 total hip arthroplasties) from 2012 to 2021
articles.outcomes: Cement usage by region and hospital type; revision surgery; periprosthetic fracture; mortality
articles.take_home: Only 40% of patients received cemented implants despite guidelines recommending them, with large variation across US states and regions. Cemented fixation reduced the risk of implant loosening and fracture around the implant, though it was associated with higher mortality, which may reflect differences in which patients received each treatment.

articles.title: One-, 1.5-, or Two-Stage Revision for Periprosthetic Hip and Knee Joint Infection? A Network Meta-Analysis Comparing Revision Strategies.
articles.authors: Selim A, Ibrahim A, Saeed A, Khamdan K, Farhan-Alanie MM, Sadiq S, et al.
articles.study_type: Network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials and comparative cohort studies
articles.population: Patients with chronic periprosthetic joint infection following hip or knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Reinfection rates, reoperation rates, infection control success, overall complications, and aseptic loosening
articles.take_home: The 1.5-stage revision procedure had the best infection control results but carried a higher risk of the implant loosening over time. One-stage revision had fewer overall complications, whilst two-stage revision was least likely to experience loosening but had higher reinfection rates.

articles.title: Trends in Racial and Socioeconomic Differences in Cementless Total Knee Arthroplasty Utilization Among Medicare Beneficiaries from 2016 to 2022.
articles.authors: Ricca GW, Torres RB, Wong L, Van Hyfte G, Dhanjani SA, Shatkin MS, et al.
articles.study_type: Observational study of national trends using Medicare claims data
articles.population: Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries undergoing primary elective total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Proportion of cementless versus cemented total knee arthroplasty procedures by race and socioeconomic status from 2016 to 2022
articles.take_home: Cementless knee replacements increased from 2.4% to 9.9% of procedures between 2016 and 2022. However, Black and Hispanic patients, particularly those with lower income, were less likely to receive cementless implants compared to White patients with higher income, though the differences were small.

articles.title: The 2026 ESSKA-ESA formal consensus on partial-thickness posterosuperior rotator cuff tears (Part 1): Definitions, classifications, etiologies, natural history and diagnosis.
articles.authors: Kany J, Iban MAR, Rosso C, Peach C, Metais P, Dias CM, et al.
articles.population: Patients with partial-thickness posterosuperior rotator cuff tears
articles.outcomes: Evidence-based consensus recommendations on definition, classification, natural history and diagnosis of partial-thickness posterosuperior rotator cuff tears
articles.take_home: Experts agree that partial-thickness rotator cuff tears should be classified by location, depth and which tendon is involved, and that these injuries have multiple causes and unpredictable progression. Current imaging tests have limitations in fully characterising these tears.

articles.title: Select large language models outperform hip preservation experts on consensus-based hip preservation questionnaire.
articles.authors: Morris K, Ottl F, Pruneski JA, Zsidai B, Hirschmann MT, Samuelsson K, et al.
articles.population: Hip preservation specialists (experts) and three large language models
articles.sample_size: 10 hip preservation experts; 3 LLMs each answering 21-item questionnaire
articles.outcomes: Overall accuracy, percentage agreement, consistency and justification quality of LLM responses compared to expert panel on consensus-based hip preservation questions
articles.take_home: Two of the three AI language models answered questions about hip conditions more accurately than a panel of hip preservation experts, achieving 100% and 98.4% accuracy compared to 90.5% for experts. AI systems showed greater consistency in their answers, though experts emphasised that AI should support rather than replace specialist doctors.

articles.title: Revision anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction following failure of combined anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with lateral extra-articular procedures: A scoping review.
articles.authors: Duru DO, O'Brien CC, Bouchard MD, Vivekanantha P, Hantouly A, de Sa D, et al.
articles.population: Adult and paediatric patients undergoing revision anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction following failure of combined ACLR with lateral extra-articular procedures
articles.sample_size: 23 patients explicitly identified as undergoing revision or re-revision from 9 included studies
articles.outcomes: Surgical revision strategies, graft selection, management of lateral extra-articular procedures, knee stability and functional outcomes
articles.take_home: There is very limited evidence on how best to revise failed ACL reconstruction when a lateral extra-articular procedure was also done initially. Surgeons currently use different approaches depending on individual patient factors and their own experience, and there is an urgent need for more consistent reporting of these complex cases.

articles.title: Hip and groin pain in physically active adults with a focus on terminology, clinical examination and imaging: A formal ESSKA-EHPA-ESMA Consensus.
articles.authors: Holmich P, Weir A, Papadopoulou T, Papavasiliou A, Thorborg K, Canata GL, et al.
articles.study_type: Formal consensus statement with expert panel review
articles.population: Athletes and physically active adults with hip and groin pain
articles.sample_size: 57 experts from 22 countries (steering group 15, rating group 20, reader group 22)
articles.outcomes: Consensus recommendations on terminology for hip and groin pain, clinical examination techniques, and imaging protocols
articles.take_home: Experts recommend using consistent terminology (such as adductor-related or hip joint-related pain) and a structured clinical examination including gait assessment, specific tests and range of motion checks. Imaging should be used as a second-line tool only after clinical examination and should always be interpreted alongside the patient's history and examination findings.

articles.title: A novel classification system for measuring and interpreting tibial tunnel morphology for revision ACLR.
articles.authors: Kennedy MI, Tollefson LV, Kennedy NI, LaPrade CM, LaPrade RF
articles.population: Patients with failed anterior cruciate ligament reconstructions presenting for revision surgery
articles.outcomes: Reproducible classification system for tibial tunnel morphology on CT imaging, with five sagittal types (tubular, shovel, balloon, dual tunnel, mushroom) and three axial types based on distance from native ACL footprint
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a reliable way to measure and categorise the shape of old knee tunnels on CT scans, which could help identify which patients are more likely to need revision knee surgery in future.

articles.title: Association of polyethylene type with revision and dislocation risk following primary total hip arthroplasty: a population-based cohort study from the Danish Hip Arthroplasty Register.
articles.authors: Chabaita M, Iljazi A, Sorensen MS, Eriksson F, Overgaard S, Petersen MM
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: All-cause revision, dislocation, and cause-specific revision (dislocation, infection, aseptic loosening) according to polyethylene type and femoral head size
articles.take_home: Highly cross-linked polyethylene was associated with lower rates of dislocation, revision surgery, and infection in patients receiving larger implant heads (36 mm and 32 mm), but showed no benefit for smaller 28 mm heads. The findings suggest potential advantages of this type of polyethylene, though more research is needed to confirm these results.
